eventCategoryDiskPressureDescription: The node is running low on disk space.
eventCategoryEvictedDescription: A pod eviction was recorded; the specific cause was not retained.
eventCategoryTemporaryStorageProvisionin: Temporary storage is being provisioned for the workspace.
eventCategoryTemporaryStorageAttachmentD: Temporary storage is being attached to the workspace.
eventCategoryVolumeUnavailableDescriptio: A required volume is not available yet.
eventCategoryEphemeralStorageDescription: A temporary-storage event was recorded; the specific cause was not retained.
eventCategoryMemoryPressureDescription: The node is running low on memory, and processes may run slowly or be restarted.
eventCategoryPidPressureDescription: The node is running low on process slots, so new processes may fail to start.
eventCategoryContainerBackoffDescription: A container, such as the Web Shell, exited and Kubernetes is waiting before restarting it. If this repeats, restart the workspace.
eventCategoryImagePullDescription: The workspace image is still downloading. Large images can take several minutes before the workspace can start.
eventCategorySchedulingDescription: Kubernetes is looking for a node with enough free capacity for the workspace. Startup resumes automatically once a node is assigned.
eventCategoryHealthCheckDescription: A workspace health probe failed. The workspace may still be starting; if it stays unready, restart it.
eventCategoryOtherDescription: The platform has not provided a displayable specific cause for this event. If the workspace makes no progress for a long time, contact an administrator with the time and reason code shown below.
eventDiagnosticContainerLocalLimit: Container {{container}} used more local temporary storage than its {{limit}} limit.
eventDiagnosticContainerLocalLimitEvicte: Container {{container}} exceeded its local temporary storage limit of {{limit}} and was evicted.
eventDiagnosticPodLocalLimit: The pod's total local temporary storage exceeded its {{limit}} limit.
eventDiagnosticNodeEphemeralPressure: The node is running low on local temporary storage.
eventDiagnosticNodeMemoryPressure: The node is running low on memory.
eventDiagnosticNodePidPressure: The node has little remaining PID capacity.
eventReasonFailedSyncDescription: The kubelet could not bring the pod to its desired state, so some containers may not have started yet. Kubernetes keeps retrying automatically.
eventReasonNodeNotReadyDescription: The node running the workspace reported not-ready. Workloads on it may pause or be rescheduled; startup continues once the node or a replacement is ready.
eventReasonFailedPostStartHookDescriptio: A container's post-start lifecycle hook did not complete. Kubernetes may restart the affected container; if this repeats, check the workspace's startup commands.
eventReasonFailedCreatePodSandboxDescrip: Kubernetes could not create the pod's sandbox (its network and isolation environment), so containers cannot start yet. The platform retries automatically; repeated occurrences usually need an administrator to inspect the node or networking.
eventReasonFailedCreateDescription: Kubernetes failed to create a resource required by the workspace. The platform retries automatically; if it persists, contact an administrator with the reason code shown below.
eventReasonFailedBindingDescription: Kubernetes failed to bind a resource the workspace needs, such as binding a pod to a node or a persistent volume to its claim. The platform retries automatically; if it persists, contact an administrator with the reason code shown below.
eventReasonDeadlineExceededDescription: An operation took longer than its allowed deadline and was aborted. Kubernetes may retry; if the workspace keeps timing out, contact an administrator.
eventReasonExceededGracePeriodDescriptio: The workload did not stop within its expected grace period. Termination may still be in progress; if it persists, an administrator may need to inspect the container runtime.
eventSchedulingBlockerCpuCapacityDescrip: The scheduler reports that candidate nodes lack enough unreserved CPU to fit the workspace request. This is scheduling capacity, not current CPU usage. Free reserved capacity, lower the request, or add suitable capacity.
eventSchedulingBlockerMemoryCapacityDesc: The scheduler reports that candidate nodes lack enough unreserved memory to fit the workspace request. This is scheduling capacity, not current memory usage. Free reserved capacity, lower the request, or add suitable capacity.
eventSchedulingBlockerStorageCapacityDes: The scheduler reports insufficient storage capacity for the requested volume on candidate nodes. Free storage, reduce the requested size, or add suitable storage capacity.
eventSchedulingBlockerNodeAffinityDescri: Some nodes do not match the workspace placement rules. Review placement and node labels together with the other reported scheduling constraints.
eventSchedulingBlockerVolumeAffinityDesc: Some nodes do not match the persistent volume topology. An administrator should check volume placement and capacity on nodes that satisfy its topology.
eventSchedulingBlockerTaintDescription: Some nodes have taints that the workspace does not tolerate. An administrator should check these taints and workspace tolerations together with the other scheduling constraints.
eventSchedulingBlockerNodeUnavailableDes: The scheduler reports unavailable or unschedulable candidate nodes. Restore suitable nodes or change placement; other reported constraints may also need attention.
adminOnly: This area is for system administrators and administrators of the current organization.
noQuotaPermission: System and organization administrators can change quota.
jobWorkerConcurrencyHelp: Controls asynchronous Kubernetes, database, and webhook jobs. It does not affect AI requests. Changes apply live without a restart.
cpuOvercommitRatioHelp: Default: 10. Whole number from 1 to 1000; 1 preserves the template’s original CPU reservations. For new workspaces, divides CPU scheduling reservations for main, sidecar and init containers: 1000m becomes 100m at 10. Each workspace keeps its creation value. Existing workspaces are not changed or restarted; CPU limits and memory reservations and limits stay unchanged. A template YAML override takes precedence.
invalidCpuOvercommitRatio: CPU overcommit ratio must be a whole number between 1 and 1000.
invalidJobWorkerConcurrency: Job worker concurrency must be a whole number between 1 and 256.
runLocationsHelp: Run locations are node selection rules: a location decides which cluster nodes may run a workspace. Requiring or preferring nodes does not reserve capacity — actual node and storage availability is checked when the workspace starts.
deleteRunLocationConfirm: Delete this disabled run location? Deletion is rejected while any template or workspace still references it.
runLocationNameHelp: Stable identifier referenced by templates and workspaces, for example gpu-west. Lowercase letters, digits, and dashes; it cannot change after creation.
runLocationNameInvalid: Use up to 63 lowercase letters, digits, or dashes; start with a letter and end with a letter or digit.
runLocationDisplayNameInvalid: Enter a display name of up to 80 UTF-8 bytes without control characters or surrounding whitespace.
runLocationEnabledHelp: A disabled location stays assigned to existing workspaces but cannot be chosen for new ones.
runLocationRequiredHostsHelp: One hostname per line. Workspaces in this location run only on these nodes.
runLocationPreferredHostsHelp: One hostname per line. The scheduler prefers these nodes when they have room; preference does not guarantee capacity.
runLocationSelectorHelp: One key=value per line. Nodes must carry every listed label to match this location.
runLocationSelectorInvalid: Use one key=value per line with valid label characters.
runLocationHostsInvalid: Enter one valid hostname per line (letters, digits, dots, dashes, or underscores).

storagePolicyHelp: High-speed storage for workspace data that can be recreated. The persistent disk is configured under resources.
workspaceTemporaryStorageHelp: Used for data that can be recreated: the default TMP directory, temporary build files, and caches such as Cargo build output and npm cache. Keep important code and personal files in the separately configured persistent Home.
workspaceTemporaryStorageInvalid: Temporary disk capacity must be a whole number from 1 to 2048 GiB.
workspaceUseLonghornHelp: By default Home uses fast local thin storage. Enabling stores the persistent Home on Longhorn with two real-time replicas; mounting and syncing can slow workspace startup. Temporary storage always stays local.
workspaceRunLocationHelp: Choose which run location provides the nodes for this workspace. Keeping the template default is usually sufficient; a location only defines node selection rules — actual capacity and storage availability are separate.
workspaceRunLocationChooseTemplate: Choose a template to see its available run locations.
workspaceRunLocationFixed: This template restricts workspaces to this location.
workspaceRunLocationNone: No run location is available for this template. Ask an administrator to enable a location allowed by the template before creating the workspace.
workspaceRunLocationInvalid: Choose a run location allowed by the template.
workspaceRunLocationUnavailable: Run locations are not loaded. Retry loading them before creating a workspace.
temporaryStorageReleased: Released while the workspace is stopped
temporaryStorageHelp: High-speed storage for workspace data that can be recreated. It is cleared when the workspace is recreated; the persistent disk is separate.

defaultNodePoolHelp: Used when workspace creation keeps the template default.

portMappingWorkspaceNotReady: Port mappings become available when the workspace is running.

deleteOrganizationConfirm: Delete the current organization? Delete its templates and workspaces first.

memberRemoveConfirm: Remove this member from the organization? They will lose access to organization resources.
memberRemoveSelfConfirm: You are removing yourself from this organization and will lose access immediately. Continue?
workspaceNameInvalid: Enter a workspace name of up to 120 characters.
workspaceResourcesInvalid: Resources cannot be below the template's minimum requests.
shrinkStorageHelp: Shrink the Home volume (persistent disk), the temporary storage, or both. The workspace stops while data is copied offline and verified, then starts again automatically. The original volumes are kept until verification succeeds; a failure rolls back without destroying any data.
shrinkStorageDowntime: Downtime notice: the workspace is unavailable from the moment it stops until the copy finishes and it resumes.
shrinkStorageKeepHint: Leave a field empty to keep its current size; enter a new size for at least one volume.
shrinkStorageUnknownUsage: Usage is unknown, so the target fit is not promised here; the backend verifies it before copying.
shrinkStorageContinues: The shrink keeps running if you close this dialog.
shrinkStorageSucceeded: Storage shrink completed. The workspace is starting again automatically.
shrinkStorageSucceededStopped: Storage shrink completed. The workspace stays stopped, as it was before the operation.
shrinkStorageFailed: The storage shrink failed and was rolled back; the original volumes were kept and no data was destroyed.
shrinkErrorInvalid: Enter a whole number of GiB of 1 or more.
shrinkErrorNotSmaller: The new size must be smaller than the current size.
shrinkErrorBelowUsage: The new size must be larger than the current usage.
shrinkStorageRetained: Data was copied, verified, and switched to the new volumes, but the original volumes are still kept — no storage has actually been freed yet. Reclaim them once you are sure.
shrinkStorageReclaimWarning: Reclaiming permanently deletes the original volumes. This cannot be undone.
shrinkStorageReclaimed: The old volumes were reclaimed; the storage space is actually freed now.
shrinkReclaimFailed: Reclaiming the old volumes failed: workspace data is unaffected and the original volumes are still kept.
shrinkRecoveryFailed: The copy was verified and switched over, but the workspace could not be restored on the new volumes. Both old and new volumes are kept and the workspace stays stopped.
shrinkStorageAutoReclaim: Automatically reclaim the old volumes after verification
shrinkStorageAutoReclaimWarning: Once enabled, the original volumes are permanently deleted as soon as the copy verifies — no second confirmation, irreversible, and the operation continues even if you close this page.
